kind: HelmRelease
metadata:
  name: neo4j
  namespace: neo4j
spec:
  interval: 1h
  releaseName: neo4j
  chart:
    spec:
      chart: neo4j
      version: "2026.7.1"
      sourceRef:
        kind: HelmRepository
        name: neo4j
        namespace: flux-system
  install:
    createNamespace: true
  values:
    # Several templates call `lookup` to reuse an existing Secret. Lookups
    # return empty during a dry-run, so the rendered auth Secret differs between
    # the diff and the apply and the release never settles.
    disableLookups: true

    neo4j:
      name: neo4j
      edition: community
      # Left empty the chart generates a random password on install and stores
      # it in a Secret, which makes the release non-reproducible -- a re-install
      # invalidates every client. This is a local sandbox with no secret
      # management, the same reason kagent ships a plaintext Postgres DSN.
      password: "abox-neo4j"
      resources:
        cpu: "500m"
        memory: "2Gi"

    volumes:
      data:
        # REQUIRED by the chart; there is no default. KinD's local-path
        # provisioner is the default StorageClass.
        mode: defaultStorageClass
        defaultStorageClass:
          accessModes:
            - ReadWriteOnce
          requests:
            storage: 5Gi

    # neo4j/mcp's get-schema calls apoc.meta.*. APOC core ships inside the
    # image; this is what moves it into plugins/ at container start.
    env:
      NEO4J_PLUGINS: '["apoc"]'

    # Loading the jar is not enough -- apoc.meta.schema reads internal store
    # APIs, so without these it registers as unavailable:
    #
    #   Neo.ClientError.Procedure.ProcedureRegistrationFailed
    #   (apoc.meta.schema is unavailable)
    config:
      dbms.security.procedures.unrestricted: "apoc.*"
      dbms.security.procedures.allowlist: "apoc.*"

    services:
      neo4j:
        # The chart defaults this to a LoadBalancer for Neo4j Browser. KinD has
        # one LB address and agentgateway already holds it, so this would sit
        # Pending forever. The ClusterIP Service the chart always creates is
        # what in-cluster clients use:
        #
        #   bolt://neo4j.neo4j:7687     HTTP http://neo4j.neo4j:7474
        #
        # For Browser, port-forward: kubectl port-forward -n neo4j svc/neo4j 7474 7687
        enabled: false

kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: llama-cpp-embeddings
  namespace: llama-cpp
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: llama-cpp-embeddings
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: llama-cpp-embeddings
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: llama-server
          # The prebuilt embedder image, published to this repo's GHCR
          # namespace. nomic-embed-text-v1.5 GGUF baked at /models/model.gguf,
          # on a llama.cpp server base.
          #
          # Two properties of this specific image that matter:
          #
          #   amd64 ONLY -- it is a single manifest, not an index. Fine on
          #   Codespaces and any x86 node; it will NOT run natively on an arm64
          #   Mac. images/nomic-embed/Dockerfile builds a multi-arch f16
          #   equivalent if that is needed.
          #
          #   Its baked CMD is only --host/--port/--embeddings/--model. The
          #   --ctx-size, --ubatch-size and --parallel below are NOT defaults --
          #   without them llama.cpp serves a single slot at a much smaller
          #   context. They have to stay on the Deployment.
          #
          # The model layer is ~134MB, so this is a quantized GGUF rather than
          # f16. That matches the deployment it was copied from, which is what
          # makes its vectors comparable with the cells that deployment
          # embedded.
          image: ghcr.io/den-vasyliev/abox/nomic-embed:v1.18.1-4ccc0ff
          # No command: -- the upstream ENTRYPOINT is the llama-server binary
          # and its path varies between image variants.
          args:
            - --host
            - 0.0.0.0
            - --port
            - "8090"
            # Without this the server exposes completions, not /v1/embeddings.
            - --embeddings
            # 16384 / --parallel 8 = 2048 tokens per slot, which is nomic's full
            # context window. --ubatch-size must be >= a slot because a pooled
            # embedding has to fit in a single micro-batch; it is the real
            # per-request ceiling here, not --ctx-size.
            - --ctx-size
            - "16384"
            - --ubatch-size
            - "2048"
            - --model
            - /models/model.gguf
            - --parallel
            - "8"
          ports:
            - containerPort: 8090
              name: http
          # The GGUF is mmap'd and loads in ~2s, so the budget only has to cover
          # scheduling: 5s x 12 = 60s.
          startupProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 8090
            periodSeconds: 5
            failureThreshold: 12
          readinessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 8090
            periodSeconds: 10
          livenessProbe:
            httpGet:
              path: /health
              port: 8090
            periodSeconds: 30
          # Exactly a production llama.cpp embedder sidecar's resources, confirmed
          # against the running pod:
          #
          #   $ kubectl top pod -n the reference embedder deployment --containers
          #   triage-controller-...   embedder   1m   81Mi
          #
          # ~75Mi resident for the same model vLLM needs 2466Mi for -- the GGUF
          # is mmap'd, so the weights barely count against RSS. The 512Mi
          # request is already generous; CPU is the real throughput lever, and
          # under node contention a query embed measured 52ms vs 4ms on a
          # laptop core, which is why the request is 500m and not 100m.
          resources:
            requests:
              cpu: 500m
              memory: 512Mi
            limits:
              cpu: "2"

[{"payload":{"chunk":0,"chunks":2,"doc":"8d5e55c6-8f98-4766-a2f5-14b93dc6bc42","document":"apiVersion: kagent.dev/v1alpha2
kind: Agent
metadata:
  name: retrieval-agent
  namespace: kagent
spec:
  type: Declarative
  description: Ingests and retrieves data across a vector store and a graph.
  declarative:
    # The ModelConfig the kagent chart creates, which every other agent here
    # uses. It was gemini-gemini-2-5-flash, but that object was never shipped
    # in releases/ -- it was created by hand and did not survive the cluster
    # being rebuilt, leaving the agent stuck on ReconcileFailed.
    # OpenAI gpt-4.1-mini, set in releases/kagent.yaml; k8s-agent runs on it too.
    modelConfig: default-model-config
    stream: true
    systemMessage: |
      You are a data agent over two stores in this cluster. Which products
      back them is not your concern and can change; the tools are the contract.

      - A vector store, via qdrant-store / qdrant-find. Free text in, semantic
        search out. The collection is chosen by the server, not by you.
      - A graph, via get-schema / read-cypher / write-cypher. Entities and the
        relationships between them.

      ## Vector store

      qdrant-store takes `information`, the text to embed, and `metadata`, a
      flat object stored with it. qdrant-find takes `query` and returns up to
      five entries, closest first, each with its content and metadata. There
      is no score and no way to ask for more: if the five are wrong, the query
      was wrong.

      The embedding model reads about the first 200 words of an entry and
      ignores the rest. Whatever is not near the top of an entry cannot be
      found by searching for it.

      When you store:
      - One entry per object. Open `information` with a plain-English sentence
        that says what the object is and what it does, then the salient spec.
        Leave out status, managedFields and anything a controller filled in.
      - Always set metadata `key` ("<namespace>/<name>", as in the graph),
        `kind`, `name` and `namespace`.

      When you search:
      - Phrase `query` as a sentence describing the object or the setting you
        want, in plain English. Not a keyword list, not a YAML fragment.
      - If no entry answers the question, rephrase once with different terms:
        the product, the field name, the purpose. Then stop.
      - Judge an entry by its content, not by its rank. Cite the metadata `key`
        of every entry an answer rests on.

      ## Ingest

      Manifests come from the k8s-agent delegate. Ask it for the YAML of the
      objects you were told to ingest; it is the only tool here that can read
      the cluster.

      Ingest declared objects, not the ones a controller generated from them.
      For kagent that means the custom resources -- kagent.dev Agent,
      ModelConfig, MCPServer, RemoteMCPServer -- and never the Deployment,
      Secret or ServiceAccount that appear alongside them. Those carry no
      authored intent and bury the graph in edges nobody asked a question
      about. The references worth modelling are in spec: an Agent's
      spec.declarative.modelConfig and spec.declarative.tools[].

      1. Call get-schema first. Reuse existing labels and relationship types;
         invent new ones only when nothing fits.
      2. Model the graph like this, and only like this:
         - One node per object, labelled with its Kubernetes kind: Agent,
           ModelConfig, MCPServer, RemoteMCPServer, HelmRelease, Gateway,
           HTTPRoute, and so on.
         - Key every node on a single `key` property, "<namespace>/<name>", and MERGE
           on that property alone:

             MERGE (n:Agent {key: "kagent/k8s-agent"})
             SET n.name = "k8s-agent", n.namespace = "kagent", n.apiVersion = "..."

           MERGE o

        name: neo4j

      # it in a Secret, which makes the release non-reproducible -- a re-install
